chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyub, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When one of you fasts the three days of the month, he should not dispute with anyone, nor act ignorantly, nor be hasty to swear and make oaths by Allah. If anyone acts ignorantly towards him, let him bear it (patiently).

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: the three days (referring to the 13th, 14th, and 15th of the lunar month)
key_terms.يُسْرِعْ إِلَى الْحَلْفِ: he should not be hasty to swear

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes for a Muslim during the three days of fasting in the month?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes that the spiritual discipline of fasting extends beyond abstention from food to include moral restraint, specifically warning against hasty swearing of oaths which can invalidate the fast's spiritual purity. It highlights the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and *hilm* (forbearance) as integral components of worship, instructing the fasting individual to absorb insults rather than engage in futile argumentation. This practice aligns with the concept of *Jihad al-Nafs* (struggle against the self), where controlling one's tongue and temper is considered as significant as physical abstinence.
